classification.difficultyReason: Read ordinates from the supplied cosine curve and reverse the reading process to locate both intersections at each specified height.

content.prompt: This graph shows $\cos\theta$. Use it to estimate the following to 2 d.p.

spec.sourceRegion: Q1 supplied graph between the stem and parts a–d
spec.description: Cosine curve on an unshaded rectangular grid, centred above the four response cells. Q2 also refers to this graph.
spec.mathematics: y=cos(theta), with theta in degrees; grid steps 10 degrees and 0.1. Labelled horizontal ticks 90, 180, 270 and 360; labelled vertical ticks -1, -0.5, 0.5 and 1. Curve has a right continuation arrow.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied curve, axes, ticks and grid remain visible; no answer readings or solution guides appear.

answer.worked:
Read the height of the cosine curve at $\theta=35^{\circ}$.
$$\cos35^{\circ}\approx0.82$$

Read the height of the cosine curve at $\theta=190^{\circ}$.
$$\cos190^{\circ}\approx-0.98$$

Read the height of the cosine curve at $\theta=330^{\circ}$.
$$\cos330^{\circ}\approx0.87$$

Read the height of the cosine curve at $\theta=140^{\circ}$.
$$\cos140^{\circ}\approx-0.77$$

children.prompt: Use the same graph to estimate the values of $\theta$ between $0^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$ for the following. Give non-exact angle estimates to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
Read the two intersections of the cosine curve with the horizontal line $y=0.8$, then project them onto the angle axis.

$\theta\approx37^{\circ}$ or $323^{\circ}$.

Read the two intersections of the cosine curve with the horizontal line $y=0.6$, then project them onto the angle axis.

$\theta\approx53^{\circ}$ or $307^{\circ}$.

The cosine curve crosses the angle axis at $90^{\circ}$ and $270^{\circ}$.

$\theta=90^{\circ}$ or $270^{\circ}$.

Read the two intersections of the cosine curve with the horizontal line $y=-0.4$, then project them onto the angle axis.

$\theta\approx114^{\circ}$ or $246^{\circ}$.
